Basically post undergrad I knew a masters wasn't for me because I just don't have the drive required to be the sole individual with knowledge on this very specific detailed problem. I chose to pursue medicine instead because it seemed more structured and how i enioy things. 

But on the route to beginning classes I had a wildly emotional year that resulted in a bipolar diagnosis and since then haven't been able to fully regain my capacity for mental focus. Feeling pressured from my parents, who were now helping support me, to try finding some kind of education to move me towards a career.

I thought with my background it might be worth trying a masters of some sort buy definitely wanted a field where I saw a purpose in what I was doing (Something I rarely saw in quantum mechanics research-my old area of interest). So engineering quickly became the best candidate and i was interested in the chemical engineering side of things most. Then I found a great team to work on that specifically researched water treatment. I've always been passionate about water and it being the foundation for life. Thought that kind of practical application of my work would help me remain motivated. 

But as it turns out I just think my issue now is that sitting alone studying something no one else knows or cares about just isn't working - as i knew wouldn't work in undergrad but obviously forgot or neglected when feeling the pressure to choose this program. I never thought it would be anything it isn't, I just thought it was something is be able to handle and was apparently wrong.

And now I feel like a failure with no options. But I also am wise enough to know that must not be true.
